$doc: The core's machine (xpute spec/machine.schema.json): the memory a device gives it,
its stack, its rings and the GPU it asks for.
`turn_posts` is what the core's turn may post besides its replies: a sensor's start
or stop each, the snapshot, the view, the files' imports at their most and a call's slot
(door.rs `EVENTS`, which it checks against this).
`bytes`: what a desktop is asked to reserve, then a handheld. A handheld's is half of
the desktop's, because a reservation is committed lazily by the OS but JavaScriptCore
reports the whole of it as the page's JavaScript memory — a Safari heap timeline read
it as one ArrayBuffer. The smaller is also the floor the module declares to the
engine (`--initial-memory`), so a page that reserves less fails to instantiate rather
than booting into a core with nowhere to put the terrain.
`region_bytes`: a reservation is a whole number of these and the bytes past the last
one are left out.
`min_heap_bytes`: the heap a phone is guaranteed, and so what everything in front of
it is checked against: the front, the module's data and the fixed ranges together
must leave this much of the smaller size. Measured from where the heap begins, so
the question is asked twice: at compile time against the lowest the heap could start
(the front's end plus the fixed ranges, xpute-core machine.rs `check`), so a terrain
grown past a phone fails to build; and at boot against where it actually started and
what the device gave.
256 MiB. The fixed ranges take 88.31 MiB, the terrain's 78.99 MiB of them.
The heap's bounded flows at their worst are checked against it at compile time too
(door/layout.rs `HEAP_FLOWS_BYTES`): the runs that `BODY_SLOTS` terrain and Earth
bodies fill (sys/io/body.rs), a body on every credit in the buddy's block for a
division's, the ways' pool at its cap, and the profiler's lanes while its setting is
on, each in the buddy's blocks, a power of two, 164.56 MiB.
Each figure here in MiB to two places is held to the code by a test
(door/layout.test.rs); the data's end is a build's, and read off one.
`module_bytes`: the stack, at the bottom of the memory, first so that an overflow
goes below zero, wraps as an unsigned 32-bit address and lands outside the memory,
which traps. With the stack after the data it would write over `.data` silently
instead. There is no MMU here and so no guard page: the wraparound is the whole of
the protection.
`thread_bytes`: the core's thread's stack on a device, where the core is a library
on a thread of its own: a main thread's 8 MiB, since React Native's JavaScript thread
has 1 MiB and wgpu's depth has no bound to state.
`slot_bytes`: a page, since a SOURCE_DECLARE's or a SCENE_CHAT's packet can come near one.
`sq_cap`: sized to what a turn is sent, not to a burst: a full ring loses nothing,
since the runtime rings with a deadline of 0 until there is room (@xpute/runtime/ipc/doorbell.ts).
And small because every slot ends up resident: a position only grows, so each slot is
written in turn.
`cq_cap`: everything one turn leaves, since the runtime reads it dry before it rings
again: a reply to each command it applies and `turn_posts`, so a drain never stops
partway. Nothing is overrun if it is short: a command whose posts and reply would not
fit waits for the next turn (xpute-core ipc/door.rs).
Its roots: the bakes' tiles, the shipped assets, the platform's storage and the placed objects' source (ts/client/src/sys/fs/namespace.ts).
The renderer's stream (pxl-render gpu/api.rs): `bytes` what one turn may send the
device, then at its end the encoder's handle table, a product number said rather than
derived. The stream says its own head. The device must have a depth-stencil format
the renderer draws with, and takes timestamps where the adapter has them.
